newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end down despite JGBs' rise.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end down despite JGBs' rise.

text.p: April 21 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.05 99.07
Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Monday's TIFFE day session slightly down despite small gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The December settled at 99.05, after trading between 99.05 and 99.07. Turnover was only 11,196 lots.
"A rise in JGB futures didn't provide much support today," a city bank trader said.
Key June JGB futures ended up 0.06 at 126.91.
"Euroyen futures' upside was heavy due to higher cash rates, which are facing upward pressure ahead of the holiday season," the city bank trader said.

The Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation on Monday morning, indicating an accommodative stance. The money market was in surplus of about 190 billion yen going into the day.
However, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.53 percent in the afternoon, after trading at 0.52 percent in the morning.
Traders predict Monday's weighted average of the overnight rate to be either 0.51 or 0.52 percent, up from Friday's 0.47 percent.
Unsecured overnight call money was higher due to a shortage of funds stemming from factors such as JGB issues.

Traders said heavy trades seen in June euroyen futures put options with a strike price of 99.25 on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) were partly responsible for capping euroyen futures.
About 11,000 lots of these options, due to expire on June 16, were traded on SIMEX.
On TIFFE, June euroyen futures settled at 99.35 on Monday.

"A lot of people are predicting the yield curve will flatten in the near future. Buying of June euroyen put options, as well as that of June JGB put options last week, may be trades based on such views," said the city bank trader.
Last week, JGB put options with a strike price of 123.00 and 122.00 were heavily traded in Tokyo. There was a rumour that hedge funds may be behind these deals, bond traders said.
"If June JGB futures fail to rise above 127.00 after Tuesday's 10-year JGB auction, euroyen futures may test the downside," said a brokerage house trader.
Market participants were closely watching the BOJ's two-day branch managers' meeting which began on Monday. News conferences by the BOJ's regional branch managers are due at 5.45 p.m. (0845 GMT).
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were little changed across the yield curve by late Monday, traders said.

About 10 billion yen worth of two-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.54 percent. One-month CDs were offered at 0.53 percent. Three-month CDs were offered at 0.55 percent. All CD rates were flat from Friday.
-- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
